A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same LocalDPO paper with complete, readable main text and supplementary material. All 20 pages were compared; pages 2–20 have identical extracted text and rendered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments on CogVideoX and Wan2.1 (Tables 1–2), ablations (Tables 3–4), and human evaluations in the main text and supplement (Figures 4 and 7).

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark experiments, ablations, human evaluations, and supplementary qualitative results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and supplementary Algorithm 1 retain the same Bézier masks, localized corruption procedure, region-aware preference loss, and hybrid DPO/SFT objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same curated Pexels video dataset and VBench and VideoJAM evaluation prompts for text-to-video generation. Supplementary dataset coverage and qualitative scenarios are identical.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same Baseline, SFT, Vanilla DPO, and DenseDPO comparators for each backbone. Human evaluations and qualitative comparisons also retain their respective comparator sets.

E3.justification: Sections 5.2 and 5.4 retain the same model configurations, metrics, 165 VBench prompts, 540 training iterations, batch size 128, 50-step inference, and 20-participant study using 50 prompts. Supplementary preprocessing is unchanged.

E4.justification: The loss-component and preference-pair construction ablations in Tables 3–4, convergence analysis in Figure 6, and supplementary training-pair and qualitative visualizations are unchanged.

E5.justification: Seed descriptions and statistical reporting are identical. Both versions present the same point estimates and human-vote percentages without adding repeated-run summaries, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results, and qualitative examples are unchanged, including the supplement. For example, Table 1 retains LocalDPO's CogVideoX-2B aesthetic and imaging quality scores of 0.6499 and 0.7080.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–6 are identical, including latent fusion, masked error normalization, and the hybrid objective. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about efficient preference-pair construction, localized preference optimization, and improved video generation quality.

C2.justification: Interpretations of regional supervision and convergence are unchanged. Supplementary Section 11 retains the limitation that random masks lack semantic awareness and the proposed future use of detection and segmentation.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 retains the same LoRA rank, corruption range, loss weights, optimizer, and inference details. Supplementary Sections 7–8 preserve the mask settings and data filtering/captioning instructions; access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, and the bibliography are identical. The positioning relative to existing video diffusion and preference-learning methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: Page 1 changes Ying Chen's affiliation superscript from 3 to 2, matching the listed Alibaba affiliation, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. All other prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–5 retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. Page layouts are unchanged; the first-page differences are limited to front-matter text.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects an unmatched author-affiliation superscript and updates the arXiv stamp. The scientific content, supporting evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations—including the supplement—are unchanged, so this small administrative correction does not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
